title: N Queens
contract: Count arrangements of n queens on an n×n board with no shared row, column, or diagonal; 0 ≤ n ≤ 10.
optimal: return queensFast(n,0,new boolean[n],new boolean[Math.max(1,2*n)],new boolean[Math.max(1,2*n)],new ArrayList<>());
reasoning: Place one queen in each row in every possible column, then reject complete boards with conflicts.
Track occupied columns and both diagonal identifiers to reject a conflicting placement before descending.
For row r and column c, diagonals are r+c and r−c+n. Undo all three occupancy flags when backtracking. Counting requires much less output storage than listing boards.
complexity: O(n·n!) upper bound with pruning, O(n)
